label: Animal health, veterinary and animal agriculture
description: The people who respond to animal disease and animal emergencies: state animal health officials and their staff, the federal veterinary service as an outside party, practicing veterinarians, diagnostic laboratories, producers and integrators, extension, veterinary schools, county fairs and animal shelters. They work an outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza, African swine fever, foot-and-mouth disease or another foreign animal disease from suspicion to release, with premises, zones, permits, sampling schedules and depopulation and disposal trackers, and the continuity of business of unaffected producers. Extends food and agriculture (processors, recalls, food defense) and public health (zoonoses) by reference.

vocabulary.public: producers and their workers, backyard flock owners, fair exhibitors, consumers and the surrounding rural community
vocabulary.frontline: field veterinarians, animal health technicians, laboratory scientists, checkpoint staff, depopulation and disposal crews, extension specialists, shelter staff
vocabulary.operationsCenter: the incident command post or the state emergency operations center, with the permit and tracing desks

roles.name: State Veterinarian / State Animal Health Official
roles.team: Team A: State Animal Health Agency
roles.description: Orders quarantine, sets control area boundaries with the federal service, decides permits and requests a state emergency declaration.

roles.name: Incident Commander / Unified Command
roles.team: Team A: State Animal Health Agency
roles.description: Sets objectives and operational periods; the state and the federal service run a unified command.

roles.name: Federal Area Veterinarian in Charge (outside party)
roles.description: Classifies cases, authorizes indemnity and resources, and supports the incident management team.

roles.name: Epidemiology Section Chief
roles.description: Leads tracing, premises designations, zone changes and the surveillance plan.

roles.name: Operations: Quarantine and Movement Control
roles.description: Runs checkpoints, permits and movement exceptions.

roles.name: Operations: Depopulation and Disposal
roles.description: Chooses method and sequence, protects personnel, picks the disposal site and plans cleaning and disinfection.

roles.name: Veterinary Diagnostic Laboratory Director
roles.description: Prioritizes samples, reports presumptive results and ships to the national reference laboratory.

roles.name: Producer / Complex Manager / Integrator Biosecurity Manager
roles.description: Owns biosecurity, access for depopulation, continuity of business, employee health and contracts.

roles.name: Extension Specialist / Fair Manager
roles.description: Reaches backyard owners and exhibitors, cancels or holds shows and answers producer questions.

roles.name: Public Health Veterinarian / Epidemiologist
roles.description: Follows up exposed workers, arranges prophylaxis and reports human cases.

roles.name: Public Information Officer
roles.description: Issues consumer messages, producer notices and rumor control.

roles.name: County Emergency Manager
roles.description: Supports checkpoints, disposal sites and sheltering of animals.

roles.name: Animal Shelter Director / Animal Services
roles.description: Directs evacuation, pet-friendly shelter, intake and reunification.

trading partners and export certifying offices
commodity groups, cooperatives and auction markets

addedThreatFamilies.label: HPAI in commercial poultry
addedThreatFamilies.description: Highly pathogenic avian influenza is presumed positive on a commercial poultry premises; the team works from the first mortality report through zones, permits, depopulation and release.

phaseArc.title: Suspicion
phaseArc.goal: An ordinary report that might be a foreign animal disease and might be nothing.
beats: A grower reports a jump in mortality in one house and a drop in water use
A routine pullorum-typhoid sample from an unrelated flock must be set aside
An accredited veterinarian calls the state animal health office about a sample

phaseArc.title: Presumptive positive
phaseArc.goal: A network laboratory result changes the status of the premises; the clock for the plan goals starts.
beats: The state laboratory reports a presumptive positive on a swab; the sample ships to the national reference laboratory
The integrator asks whether trucks may leave the complex before confirmation

phaseArc.title: Quarantine and zones
phaseArc.goal: The premises is quarantined and the control area and surveillance zone are drawn from the plan minimums and local epidemiology.
beats: A draft control area that must reach at least 10 km beyond the infected premises
Contract growers of the same integrator sit inside the zone
A permit request to move birds already loaded for processing

phaseArc.title: Tracing and surveillance
phaseArc.goal: Contact and at-risk premises are identified, designated and put on a sampling schedule; permits keep unaffected producers working.
beats: A feed truck route that visited two premises in the last three days
The case-management system lags and designations disagree between teams

phaseArc.title: Depopulation and disposal
phaseArc.goal: Animals on infected premises are depopulated and disposed of against the plan goal, with crews, methods and sites as the limit.
beats: The plan goal is depopulation within 24 hours of the presumptive positive and the crew has half the capacity needed
The chosen disposal site is full or too far for the trucks available

phaseArc.title: Cleaning and release
phaseArc.goal: Premises are cleaned and disinfected, tested and released on stated conditions; the control area shrinks as evidence allows.
beats: Cleaning and disinfection sign-off on the first premises
Surveillance zone premises still due for sampling

phaseArc.title: Recovery and trade
phaseArc.goal: Producers restock, trading partners are told, and the hot wash records what the clocks showed.
beats: A trading partner asks for the zone map and dates
A hot wash disagreement over who set the control area boundary

decisionPointExamples: issue a permit to move product from a monitored premises now, or hold it a day for another round of negative tests
depopulate the larger infected house first or the one nearer a road with more traffic
widen the control area to include a contract grower, or hold the minimum and risk a later change
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a mortality log, a laboratory result sheet, a feed or crew visit record, a premises on a map near the zone edge, a permit request with a destination in the zone
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: the case-management system is slow, a disposal site is full, crews are short, a road checkpoint is understaffed, the laboratory has a backlog
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the state animal health office, the federal veterinary service, the integrator, the laboratory network and the county emergency manager
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Stay at the level of animal health response decisions: designations, zones, permits, sampling, depopulation and disposal logistics, messages. Use only fictional premises, farms, owners and people; place premises as fictional points, never at a real farm. Give no pathogen culture, growth or biosecurity-bypass detail. Cite the response plan edition when a rule or distance is stated, and say the state plan governs.

decisionMustMention.description: a control decision (quarantine, zone, permit, depopulation or disposal)

addedThreatFamilies.label: HPAI in dairy cattle
addedThreatFamilies.description: A positive milk sample or herd report sets off herd-level testing and movement decisions for a state; the structure follows the national milk testing strategy and the designer confirms current state rules.

phaseArc.title: Suspicion
phaseArc.goal: An ordinary report that might be a foreign animal disease and might be nothing.

A veterinarian reports a herd with reduced milk and appetite

phaseArc.title: Presumptive positive
phaseArc.goal: A network laboratory result changes the status of the premises; the clock for the plan goals starts.
beats: A herd-level test is positive on one farm and pending on two
The cooperative asks whether milk may go to the plant

phaseArc.title: Quarantine and zones
phaseArc.goal: The premises is quarantined and the control area and surveillance zone are drawn from the plan minimums and local epidemiology.
beats: A quarantine of the affected herd and a movement hold on lactating cattle leaving the state
A producer asks what testing a pre-movement certificate needs

phaseArc.title: Tracing and surveillance
phaseArc.goal: Contact and at-risk premises are identified, designated and put on a sampling schedule; permits keep unaffected producers working.
beats: Herd lists that share a trucking route and a milk hauler

phaseArc.title: Cleaning and release
phaseArc.goal: Premises are cleaned and disinfected, tested and released on stated conditions; the control area shrinks as evidence allows.
beats: Herd-level testing is repeated before the state status changes
A processor wants a written statement for its customers

phaseArc.title: Recovery and trade
phaseArc.goal: Producers restock, trading partners are told, and the hot wash records what the clocks showed.

The hot wash records which rule the designer had to confirm

decisionPointExamples: allow milk to move to the plant under a permit with testing, or hold it at the farm and lose the day
test every herd on the route now, or sample the highest-risk herds first
announce a state status change, or wait for one more round of herd-level results
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a silo result that traces to farms, a hauler route, a herd test sheet, a worker symptom log, a cooperative notice
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: the current movement rule differs between sources, a laboratory turnaround, hauler schedules, staff shortages at the testing team
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the state animal health office, the federal veterinary service, the cooperative, the processor, the public health veterinarian
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Stay at the level of animal health response decisions: designations, zones, permits, sampling, depopulation and disposal logistics, messages. Use only fictional premises, farms, owners and people; place premises as fictional points, never at a real farm. Give no pathogen culture, growth or biosecurity-bypass detail. Cite the response plan edition when a rule or distance is stated, and say the state plan governs. Dairy movement and testing rules changed during 2025 and 2026; generate from the structure of the national milk testing strategy and tell the designer to confirm current state rules.

phaseArc.title: Quarantine and zones

phaseArc.title: Workaround
